page: Amazon Web Services m5.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8175M x86_64 processor running at 3.1 GHz. The processor includes a 33 MB L3 cache and supports hardware extensions such as AVX, AVX-512F, and AES cryptography. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance profiles. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 25% tier. Conversely, multi-core performance, such as Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU scores, registers in the middle 50% average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached blocks also demonstrate average tier results, with uncached read speeds reaching 87.77 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the instance achieves average tier throughput in Redis SET operations and static web serving, while LLM inference tasks on medium-sized models show weak prompt processing but average text generation speeds.

From a resource density perspective, the m5.4xlarge provides a balanced allocation of compute and memory resources without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. This configuration is suitable for workloads that require moderate multi-threaded processing and steady memory access rather than peak single-thread speed. Appropriate workloads include general-purpose web serving, multi-threaded software compilation, database operations, and medium-scale redis caching.
